speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent, and I understand you're experiencing sudden-onset vertigo. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me if this dizziness started while you were lying down, rolling over in bed, or looking up? Also, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or difficulty speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The sudden onset of spinning vertigo lasting only 3 minutes while rolling over in bed, without hearing loss or neurological deficits, is classic for BPPV. I will now request images of your inner ear canals to confirm the presence of displaced otoconia. REQUEST IMAGES: Inner_Ear_Canal_Scan.
